If it saved you an evening of README archaeology, you can support Maddie's work, and that support is what keeps her building useful, privacy-respecting things the world forgot to make.
strings.Decomp Buddy is one of those holes. The: Decomp Buddy is one of those holes. The decomp and recomp scene is doing something remarkable - turning games that were locked to old consoles into real native PC programs - but every project ships with its own build, its own folder rules, its own idea of where your disc image goes. Maddie got tired of reading twenty READMEs to set up twenty games, so she built the thing that reads them for you, checks that the dump you picked is the one the project actually wants, and hands you a folder that just works.

strings.Some games only come as a Windows versio: Some games only come as a Windows version. On Linux and Steam Deck, Decomp Buddy plays those through Proton (the same thing Steam uses for Windows games) or Wine. It uses the Proton builds Steam already has: in Steam, search your Library for "Proton" and install one if none is listed. Each game gets its own Windows setup, so one can't break another, and you can pick a different Proton per game in its More… panel.

Some games only come as a Windows version. Wine can run many of those on a Mac: DirectX 9, DirectX 11 and OpenGL games often work; games that need Vulkan or DirectX 12 (most Xbox 360 recomps) usually don't.
